construction: tape file 5 (A-B) gains one extra record, one byte long (0x00), after its last record and before its filemark; everything after it is shifted by one record
note: Observations (catalogue E3): a Scanner with no off-tape state; the BOT walk of §8.4.1.

scanner.reasoning: Derived a4-minimal geometry: bootstrap 1 block, Object 4, sidecar 7 (H = 1, P = 4), ParityMap 3 (M = 1), each replica 3 records (payload 64 x 4 + 256 = 512 bytes, one payload record), each separation extent N records. A starts at LBA 19; the untouched layout plans EOD at 33 + 2N. The extra record moves B, BC, C and EOD by one, so the tape's EOD is 34 + 2N. Spacing back over five filemarks from EOD: C's footer is read one LBA past its recorded footer position, so it supplies no layout; BC's footer is a separation footer, not a terminal replica footer; B's footer is read one LBA past its recorded position, no layout; the record before AB's filemark is the one-byte record, a wrong-length record and therefore an invalid control candidate, not TapeIo; A's footer is at its recorded position but its layout's planned EOD (33 + 2N) lies before the tape's EOD (34 + 2N), so the layout is not used. No footer supplies a layout, so no replica validates.
scanner.then: Returns BotStructuralRecoveryRequired, performs the Section 8.4.1 walk (observation 'walk'), and reports that terminal authority was not recovered. Never an empty inventory.
quotes: locate, from EOD, the local footer of a terminal replica, and from it the planned terminal layout (Section 8.3); the Scanner spaces back over up to five filemarks from EOD and reads the record before each, stopping early when a backspace does not cross exactly one filemark or leaves the partition.

A terminal replica's footer that parses supplies a planned layout only when its recorded footer position equals the position at which it was read, and the layout's planned EOD is at or after the tape's EOD.
A layout whose planned EOD lies before the tape's EOD may be followed by later tape files, so it is not used, and when no footer supplies a layout, no replica validates;

A Reader treats it as invalid content of the component it belongs to: an invalid candidate for a control component, an erasure when the Recoverer reads a data block or parity shard (Section 13.4), and, for the first record with a supplied or known block size, the refusal of Sections 8.4 and 15.
if no replica validates, perform the BOT structural recovery walk in Section 8.4.1.

If A, B, and C all fail, the Scanner returns an explicit `BotStructuralRecoveryRequired` outcome and performs the Section 8.4.1 walk; BOT Object classifications are likewise streamed before their terminal summary.
The walk does not invent a terminal replica. The Scanner MUST report that terminal authority was not recovered.
It MUST NOT convert missing terminal authority into an empty inventory or infer the existence of a planned future component from A or B.

tape_files.1: Object candidate by elimination (item 7); identity unknown
tape_files.5: IndexSeparationExtent AB (item 3), damaged: measured N + 1 records against planned N (TerminalIndexSeparationParse); keeps its control type; walk continues
tape_files.6: TapeIndexReplica B (item 2); count agrees; begins one LBA after its planned start. Damaged or intact: open
tape_files.7: IndexSeparationExtent BC (item 3); count agrees; begins one LBA late. Damaged or intact: open
tape_files.8: TapeIndexReplica C (item 2); count agrees; begins one LBA late. Damaged or intact: open

walk.ends: EOD at the start of tape file 9
walk.validated_scope: tape files 0..3 (directory_scope_tape_file_count = 4, the ParityMap's tape file number plus one); T = 4 and W = 4 recomputed from that prefix equal the ParityMap's scope fields; files 0..3 are untouched so the projection hashes to canonical_map_digest
walk.second_pass: no change: the directory's one entry names tape file 2, already a sidecar
open_points: Whether items 2 and 3 compare the walked tape-file number or device start position with the header's planned tuple, and so whether tape files 6, 7 and 8 are reported damaged. Permitted: intact control file of that kind, or damaged control file of that kind. In either case none is an Object, and none is inside the validated scope.
quotes: Per tape file: read the head block; measure the file's length by filemark spacing (space to the next filemark; the file's block count is the position delta minus one); a zero-block file or a missing trailing filemark is structural damage; EOD at a file start ends the walk.

matching terminal-replica header magic commits the tape file to this control type. The header and measured block count are checked against the encoded component plan. A malformed frame or count mismatch is reported as a damaged terminal replica; it MUST NOT fall through to Object. When the head is unreadable, the file's last block is read, and a terminal footer whose magic matches establishes the same type, whether or not the footer parses. The footer takes the header's place in the check below: a footer that does not parse, or whose record count differs from the measured count, is reported as a damaged terminal replica.
matching separation-header magic commits the tape file to this control type under the same malformed-control and measured count rules.

In items 2 through 6, a count-mismatch “hard error” is scoped to that rung and that tape file's classification: the Scanner reports the failed classification and continues the walk with the next tape file.
Under items 2 and 3 the file keeps its control type, damaged; under items 4, 5 and 6, as under item 1, the file is not recognised, and item 7 applies.
It reports each candidate's identity as unknown unless a separate exact Object-recovery authority succeeds.

A map produced by the Section 8.4.1 walk, after the second pass of Section 12.3, is validated against the tape's final ParityMap when that ParityMap validates and is marked `is_final_directory`, and the map's canonical projection (Section 7.3) through the ParityMap's own entry hashes to its `canonical_map_digest`.
The validated scope and durable boundary are the first `directory_scope_tape_file_count` tape files, ending with that ParityMap's entry; `W` is `directory_scope_highest_protected_ordinal`.
MUST treat rows beyond the validated prefix as forensic only, never as recovery inputs.
A terminal-replica payload describes only the prefix before A, so kinds 4 and 5 inside that payload are invalid, even though a Scanner recognizes those kinds in the measured physical tail.
